title: API mutation
prompt: Update server data, handle failure, and refresh the visible record. Submit the relevant snippet or implementation notes, and validate the complete behavior in a local React/Vite project. CodeLeaf does not run arbitrary learner code.

starter.code:
const response = await fetch(`/api/tasks/${task.id}`, { method: "PATCH", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ done: true }) });
if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Could not update task");
starter.run_instructions: Copy the starter into a local React/Vite project, supply the omitted surrounding component/imports if needed, run it, and test one failure or edge case.

public_tests.name: Required concept markers
public_tests.description: A basic server-side text check confirms that the submitted snippet includes the key constructs. It does not prove the whole UI works.

acceptance_criteria: The expected interaction/result described in the prompt is observable.
The implementation uses the intended React concept rather than a hard-coded screenshot.
Normal and edge/failure cases are tested.
Labels, semantics, focus, and errors are handled where relevant.
The learner documents a reproducible local test.
hints: Build the smallest valid case first.
Compare current and expected state or output.
Try an empty, duplicate, invalid, delayed, or failed case relevant to the task.
grading_method: Static pattern check only, followed by human review of behavior against acceptance criteria. This is not arbitrary-code execution or a proof of correctness.
retry_policy: Retry is allowed; incorrect submissions award no XP. The platform awards its fixed exercise XP only when the configured server-side check first succeeds.
